our_title: PT-Scotch tools return without MPI_Finalize on help/version; errorPrint never aborts the job
ran: mpirun --oversubscribe -np 2 dgmap -h (and -V, '?', dgord/dgscat/dggath/dgtst -h): usage printed by every rank, then 'prterun has exited due to process rank 1 ... exited without calling "finalize"', rc=1; patched: rc=0 for all 15 paths. Hang test: m16x16.grf scattered on 3 ranks, part-1.grf truncated; timeout 15 mpirun -np 3 dgtst 'part-%r.grf' -> 'dgtst(1): ERROR: dgraphLoadDist: bad input (1)', job killed by prterun, rc=1 in < 1 s (same with dgord); patched with 0004: 'MPI_ABORT was invoked on rank 1 in communicator MPI_COMM_WORLD, Errorcode: 1', rc=1, 1 s.
read_only: the hang itself: Open MPI 5 / PRRTE kills the job on a non-zero exit, so the other ranks never hang here; a launcher that keeps the job alive (Slurm srun without KillOnBadExit, some batch systems) is needed to see it
severity_note: help/version exits only produce a spurious launcher error (rc 1); the error path hangs only with launchers that do not kill the job, hence low as in the review
review_accuracy: first half accurate and reproduced; the 'others can hang' claim is launcher dependent (not reproducible with Open MPI/PRRTE, which kills the job); its Fix line is what the series does
first_pass_critique: Right on both halves and honest about not reproducing the hang. It left MPI_Abort as a non-preferred sketch: the PT variant of the error-exit library already calls MPI_Initialized to print the rank, so it is MPI-aware by design and the abort belongs there (the sketch also lacked the MPI_Finalized guard, needed because MPI_Initialized stays true after MPI_Finalize). It did not note that usage is printed once per rank.

fix_options.label: a. MPI_Finalize before the three early returns of the five tools
fix_options.tested: rc 0 for dgmap -h/-V/?, dgord/dgscat/dggath/dgtst -h with -np 2; make ptcheck 32/64
fix_options.maintainer_fit: the final return of main already does MPI_Finalize(); return (EXIT_SUCCESS): this makes the early exits identical

fix_options.label: b. MPI_Abort in the PT-Scotch error-exit library
fix_options.summary: libptscotcherrexit's errorPrint calls MPI_Abort (MPI_COMM_WORLD, EXIT_FAILURE) when MPI is initialized and not finalized, then exit; the hands-on guide sentence updated.
fix_options.tested: bad part file on rank 1, -np 3: MPI_ABORT banner, rc 1 in 1 s; make ptcheck 32/64 (the dg* program tests link it)
fix_options.tradeoffs: behaviour change for embedders linking libptscotcherrexit: the whole job dies instead of one process (which is what an exit-on-error library means for an MPI job); Open MPI prints its MPI_ABORT banner
fix_options.maintainer_fit: the PT variant exists only to be MPI-aware (rank prefix at :120-126); he kept it a separate library precisely so that exit semantics can differ; kept as its own commit so it can be dropped alone

fix_options.label: c. Print usage/version on process 0 only, and finalize
fix_options.summary: Same as a, plus 'if (proclocnum == 0)' around the prints, so that -np 8 does not print 8 copies.
fix_options.tradeoffs: nicer output but changes what users see on the other ranks' streams; the '?' path runs before the rank is used elsewhere so it is safe
fix_options.maintainer_fit: cosmetic, no precedent in the tree; he can take it later if wanted

fix_options.label: d. MPI_Abort only under a compile flag
fix_options.summary: #ifdef SCOTCH_ERROR_ABORT around the abort, default off.
fix_options.tradeoffs: keeps the old behaviour by default, so the hang stays for everyone who does not know the flag
fix_options.maintainer_fit: he has SCOTCH_ERROR_SLEEP as precedent for such flags, but an opt-in does not fix the reported problem

test_added: ; no natural home: the check Makefile has no test of program exit statuses on help paths, and the hang needs a launcher that keeps the job alive
docs_updated: doc/src/handson/h_c.tex (libptscotcherrexit now 'aborts the whole MPI job')
needs_note: the hang needs a launcher that does not kill the job when a rank exits non-zero; not available (Open MPI 5 only)
notes: Patch 0004 is a design decision for the maintainer: MPI_Abort of MPI_COMM_WORLD from a library. I recommend it because the error-exit libraries are documented as 'exit immediately' and, for an MPI job, exit() of one process is undefined by the standard while MPI_Abort is the defined way; it is a separate commit.

ran: repro/mutate.sh on m16x16.grf before (combined series): (a) memset parttab to -1 before checkMap rc=0; (b) fixed vertex (0,0) moved to part 1 for the fixed cases rc=0; (c) parttab[5] = 0 on the variable-sized hypercube (terminal 0 does not exist) rc=0; (d) parttab[5] = 1000000 on it rc=0. After (0008): (a) 'checkMap: invalid mapping (1)' rc=1; (b) 'invalid mapping (3)' rc=1; (c) 'invalid mapping (2)' rc=1; (d') parttab[5] = 5 on cmplt 5 'invalid mapping (2)' rc=1. Unmutated: check_scotch_graph_map rc=0 on m4x4, m4x4_b100000, m16x16, 32-bit and 64-bit.
severity_note: same as the review: the main sequential mapping test could not detect an unmapped or moved vertex
evidence: test_scotch_graph_map.c:95-96 'if (partval == -1)                            /* Unmapped vertex */\n      continue;' ; :102-103 'if ((flagval == 0) &&\n        (partval >= partnbr)) {' ; :254 'checkMap (vertnbr, parttab, archsiz, (archnum == (ARCHNBR - 1)) ? 1 : 0);' (no record of the preset fixed parts anywhere)
review_accuracy: accurate on the three gaps; its 'bound partval by the architecture size' is wrong for variable-sized architectures (SCOTCH_archSize (vhcub) = 1 while terminal numbers are binary-tree numbers, arch_vhcub.c:243-244): the right bound is 'is a terminal domain of the architecture', which SCOTCH_archDomTerm answers for every architecture (0 is rejected for vhcub, arch_vhcub.c:102-103; >= termnbr for cmplt, arch_cmplt.c:271)
first_pass_critique: Found the three gaps and tested mutations, but its preferred bound '2 * (vertnbr + 2)' for variable-sized architectures is an empirical constant with no meaning (labels are tree numbers whose depth depends on the strategy); SCOTCH_archDomTerm is the library's own definition of a valid terminal. It did not update G12's zero-load fixed-vertex case (which it could not know of) and did not notice that the old 'partnbr/flagval' parameters become dead once the architecture is passed.
